answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce, non-reusable resource before it can influence a market, and the protocol caps voting weight per bond rather than per claimed identity. A lotus-style reputation score can grow only through settled trades with distinct, bonded counterparties; splitting one stake across many names does not multiply influence. The vault holds bonds until disputes expire, while a cipher-bound receipt prevents reuse across accounts. A sybil attacker therefore has to lock real capital for each effective identity and risks losing it for fraud.
